title: Opposite vertices of base polyhedra
statement: If every vertex of a finite-dimensional base polyhedron B lies in {-1,0,1}^n and the origin belongs to B, then B has a vertex v for which -v is also a vertex.

counterexample.description: A normalized integer submodular function whose base polyhedron contains the origin and has every vertex in {-1,0,1}^n, but whose complete greedy vertex set contains no opposite pair.
